questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should check your blind spots by
options: A) Looking into the rear view mirror.
B) Looking over your shoulder.
C) Looking at the side mirrors.
questions.answer: B) Looking over your shoulder.

questions.question: 'Blind spots' of a vehicle is an area which cannot be viewed by
options: A) the rear view mirror.
B) left and right wings mirror.
C) both A and B.
questions.answer: C) both A and B.

questions.question: Motorcyclist will often look over their right shoulder just before turning right. This is because ___
options: A) they need to listen for following traffic.
B) they need to check for traffic in their blind area.
C) looking around helps them balance as they turn.
questions.answer: B) they need to check for traffic in their blind area.

questions.question: Before you make a U-turn on the road, you should check your blind spot by
options: A)looking at the rear view mirror.
B) looking over your shoulder.
C) looking at the side mirrors.
questions.answer: B) looking over your shoulder.

questions.question: It is important to check the 'blind spot' before
options: A) changing lanes.
B) changing gear.
C) slowing down.
questions.answer: A) changing lanes.

questions.question: Your reaction time could be affected when
options: A) you are tired.
B) your vehicle is old.
C) the traffic is heavy.
questions.answer: A) you are tired.

questions.question: When driving through puddles of water on the road, you should
options: A) drive faster.
B) drive slower.
C) not change speed.
questions.answer: B) drive slower.

questions.question: Before moving off, you should
options: A) use your mirrors and signal if necessary.
B) use your mirrors, check your blind spot and signal.
C) signal and move.
questions.answer: B) use your mirrors, check your blind spot and signal.

questions.question: How does the car interior lights affect your driving?
options: A) It makes you more alert.
B) It reduces your visibility.
C) It helps you to see better.
questions.answer: B) It reduces your visibility.

questions.question: On a wet road, the braking distance will
options: A) not increase if the tyres are good.
B) not increase if the brakes are efficient.
C) increase despite good tyres.
questions.answer: C) increase despite good tyres.

questions.question: In which of these situations should you avoid overtaking?
options: A) Approaching a dip in the road.
B) On a 50km/h road.
C) In a one-way street.
questions.answer: A) Approaching a dip in the road.

questions.question: What should you use the horn for?
options: A) to signal your annoyance.
B) to greet other road users.
C) to warn others of danger.
questions.answer: C) to warn others of danger.

questions.question: When driving in heavy rain, you should turn on
options: A) The hazard lights.
B) The headlights and hazard lights.
C) The headlights and tail lights.
questions.answer: C) The headlights and tail lights.

questions.question: You must signal your intention at least
options: A) 2 seconds in advance.
B) 3 seconds in advance.
C) 5 seconds in advance.
questions.answer: B) 3 seconds in advance.

sections.title: Ambulance / Bus Lane / Zig Zag lines

questions.question: When you hear the siren of an emergency vehicle, you should
options: A) Stop immediately where you are in order to make way.
B) Pull over to the left or right side of the road.
C) Sound your horn to warn the front vehicles to speed up.
questions.answer: B) Pull over to the left or right side of the road.

questions.question: Within the zig-zag lines area of a pedestrian crossing, you;
options: A) May overtake another vehicle only when that vehicle comes to a complete stop.
B) May overtake another vehicle if you do not cause inconvenience to pedestrians.
C) Must not overtake even if you think it is safe to do so.
questions.answer: C) Must not overtake even if you think it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you hear the siren of an emergency vehicle but are not sure where it is coming from, you should
options: A) continue to drive at the same speed.
B) move to the side and stop if necessary.
C)drive faster so as not to obstruct the emergency vehicle.
questions.answer: B) move to the side and stop if necessary.

questions.question: You should give way to emergency vehicles approaching from behind by
options: A) slowing down.
B) moving to the side.
C) driving faster.
questions.answer: B) moving to the side.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle behind you sounds its siren, you should
options: A) slow down quickly.
B) pull to the side and stop if necessary.
C) increase your speed.
questions.answer: B) pull to the side and stop if necessary.

questions.question: During bus lane prohibited hours, motorist is allowed to use the bus lane when
options: A) it is empty.
B) the other lanes are congested.
C) the driver is trying to avoid a collision.
questions.answer: C) the driver is trying to avoid a collision.

questions.question: If a fire engine behind you sounds the siren, you should
options: A) Continue at normal speed.
B) Move to the side, slow down or stop if necessary.
C) Increase your speed and move to the side.
questions.answer: B) Move to the side, slow down or stop if necessary.

questions.question: On a one way street, you hear the siren of an emergency vehicle behind you, you should
options: A) Give way by moving to the left only.
B) Give way by moving to the left or right.
C) Stop immediately.
questions.answer: B) Give way by moving to the left or right.

questions.question: What must you do when a police vehicle with its siren on is behind you?
options: A) Continue to drive as normal.
B) Slow down and move to the side.
C) Speed up.
questions.answer: B) Slow down and move to the side.

questions.question: When being followed by a police vehicle with its siren on, you should
options: A) Accelerate quickly to get away from it.
B) Pull over safely, as soon as possible to let it pass.
C) Brake quickly and stop to let it pass.
questions.answer: B) Pull over safely, as soon as possible to let it pass.

questions.question: On Saturday, all vehicles must avoid the bus lane between (red marking)
options: A) 7.30 am to 8.00 pm
B) 7.30 am to 11.00 pm
C) 5.00 pm to 8.00 pm
questions.answer: B) 7.30 am to 11.00 pm

questions.question: When you cannot confirm the direction of the approach of an emergency vehicle, you should
options: A) Maintain your speed and position.
B) Increase the speed of your vehicle.
C) Slow down your speed and move to the left lane.
questions.answer: C) Slow down your speed and move to the left lane.

questions.question: While driving and  you hear the siren of an ambulance behind you, you should
options: A) Stop immediately to let the ambulance overtake or pass
B) Keep left, slow down and stop if necessary
C) Speed up in order not to obstruct the ambulance
questions.answer: B) Keep left, slow down and stop if necessary

questions.question: You are not allowed to drive into a bus lane on Monday to Friday from
You can drive on the bus lane
options: A) when all other lanes are occupied.
B) outside the restricted hours.
C) when passing another vehicle on the left.
questions.answer: B) outside the restricted hours.

questions.question: When can you use the right lane of a two-lane carriageway?
options: A) When your path of travel is obstructed by road works or parked vehicles.
B) When your speed is higher that the speed limit for the road.
C) When the right lane is free of traffic.
questions.answer: A) When your path of travel is obstructed by road works or parked vehicles.

questions.question: You may drive along the right-most lane when
options: A) You are travelling at the speed limits.
B) The traffic is not heavy.
C) You are overtaking another vehicle.
questions.answer: C) You are overtaking another vehicle.

questions.question: Road hogging
options: A) Ensures a smoother flow of traffic
B) Causes other vehicles to overtake dangerously on the left
C) Causes other vehicles to overtake on the right
questions.answer: B) Causes other vehicles to overtake dangerously on the left

questions.question: When should you use the right outer most lane of a carriageway?
options: A) When driving at the maximum speed
B) When overtaking
C) When all other lanes are occupied
questions.answer: B) When overtaking

questions.question: You are permitted to use the outer most right lane on a three-lane dual carriageway when
options: A) you are travelling at the maximum legal speed limit of the road
B) you intend to turn right ahead
C) emergency vehicles are not using it
questions.answer: B) you intend to turn right ahead

questions.question: When you see green traffic light signal from a distance, you should
options: A) Speed up.
B) Slow down.
C) Carry on at the same speed.
questions.answer: B) Slow down.

questions.question: When approaching a traffic light junction with the amber light flashing, you should
options: A) Slow down and proceed across the junction only when it is safe to do so.
B) Speed up in order to pass the junction before the light changes.
C) Stop at the stop-line and wait for the light to change.
questions.answer: A) Slow down and proceed across the junction only when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When the traffic light turns green at a junction, you should
options: A) depress the accelerator hard and move off quickly.
B) check traffic from right and left before moving off.
C) only move off when other vehicles move.
questions.answer: B) check traffic from right and left before moving off.

questions.question: A flashing amber traffic light signal means
options: A) signal is about to be cancelled
B) stop unless you are so close to the stop-line that you cannot stop safety
C) traffic lights signals are out of order
questions.answer: C) traffic lights signals are out of order

questions.question: The light turns red as you approach a traffic junction, when stopping you should
options: A) Depress the brake and the clutch pedals simultaneously
B) Shift to neutral and step on the brakes
C)Brake firmly and depress the clutch pedal as the car comes to a stop
questions.answer: C) Brake firmly and depress the clutch pedal as the car comes to a stop

questions.question: The 'two-second rule' is used in normal driving situation at
options: A) Certain speed only
B) All speed
C) Fixed speed only
questions.answer: B) All speed

questions.question: When approaching a junction and the traffic lights signal change from green to amber, you should
options: A) stop at the stop line unless you are so close that sudden or sharp braking might cause an accident.
B) speed up to clear the intersection.
C) stop only if a red light camera is in use.
questions.answer: A) stop at the stop line unless you are so close that sudden or sharp braking might cause an accident.

questions.question: When approaching a traffic light signal that has turned to amber, you should
options: A) Speed up.
B) Maintain your speed.
C) Slow down and stop.
questions.answer: C) Slow down and stop.

questions.question: When the amber traffic light is flashing continuously, you should
options: A) Slow down and proceed with caution
B) Stop and wait for it to change to green
C) Drive through it quickly
questions.answer: A) Slow down and proceed with caution

questions.question: When the 'amber' traffic light signal is flashing, you should
options: A) Carry on driving
B) Slow down and look out for other vehicles before proceeding
C) Call the police
questions.answer: B) Slow down and look out for other vehicles before proceeding

questions.question: When the traffic light signal turns 'green', you should check
options: A) For oncoming traffic before moving off
B) For oncoming traffic and traffic from the right and left before moving off
C) The rear view mirror before moving off
questions.answer: B) For oncoming traffic and traffic from the right and left before moving off

questions.question: When the traffic lights signal turns amber and you have already passed the stop line you should,
options: A) stop and reverse back to the stop line
B) continue to drive through the junction
C) stop immediately
questions.answer: B) continue to drive through the junction

questions.question: When the traffic lights signal turns amber, you should
options: A) accelerate and cross the junction
B) slow down and be ready to stop
C) proceed with caution as the traffic light signals are out of order
questions.answer: B) slow down and be ready to stop

questions.question: When you approach a 'green' traffic light signal at a junction, you should
options: A) Accelerate hard
B) Slow down and be ready to stop
C) Maintain your speed
questions.answer: B) Slow down and be ready to stop

questions.question: Before reaching a junction, you should;
options: A) Form up into the correct lane which you intend to travel.
B)Sound your horn to caution other road users.
C) Speed up so as not to cause a traffic jam.
questions.answer: A) Form up into the correct lane which you intend to travel.

questions.question: On a two-way street with two lanes in each direction, you should keep to;
options: A) the left lane.
B)the outer lane.
C) either answers.
questions.answer: A) the left lane.

questions.question: On a two-lane carriageway, you should
options: A) keep to the left lane
B) keep to the outer lane
C)not overtake another vehicle
questions.answer: A) keep to the left lane

questions.question: Switching lanes suddenly or abruptly will
options: A) improve the flow of traffic on the road.
B) cause inconvenience and danger to other motorists.
C) cause wear and tear to the vehicle.
questions.answer: B) cause inconvenience and danger to other motorists.

questions.question: To maintain good lane discipline, you should
options: A) form up correctly into the intended lane before reaching the junction
B) drive between lanes so that you can switch lane easily
C) follow closely to the vehicle in front
questions.answer: A) form up correctly into the intended lane before reaching the junction

questions.question: Under what circumstances you may not follow the 'keep left rule' ?
options: A) When travelling at the maximum speed limit of the road.
B) When traffic is light.
C) When your path is obstructed.
questions.answer: C) When your path is obstructed.

questions.question: When driving along a two-way street, you should
options: A)always keep near the centre line of the road
B) not cross the centre line at bends
C) not overtake at all times
questions.answer: B) not cross the centre line at bends

questions.question: When turning right at a one-way street, you should position your vehicle
options: A) In the right hand lane.
B) Just left of the centre of the road.
C) In any lane depending on the traffic conditions.
questions.answer: A) In the right hand lane.

questions.question: You are driving on a three-lane carriageway at 80 km/h .There is no traffic ahead. Which lane should you use ?
options: A) Any lane.
B) Middle lane.
C) Left lane.
questions.answer: C) Left lane.

questions.question: You may overtake another vehicle on the left
options: A) If it is a heavy vehicle.
B) If the driver in front signals his intention to turn right.
C) If you are certain that the vehicle would not change direction.
questions.answer: B) If the driver in front signals his intention to turn right.

questions.question: When should you start to keep left after overtaking?
options: A) As soon as you are ahead of the overtaken vehicle.
B) When you can see the overtaken vehicle in your left wing mirror.
C) When you can see the overtaken vehicle in your rear view mirror inside the cabin.
questions.answer: C) When you can see the overtaken vehicle in your rear view mirror inside the cabin.

questions.question: Before overtaking another vehicle, you should signal for at least
options: A) Three  seconds
B) Five seconds
C) Seven seconds
questions.answer: A) Three  seconds

questions.question: If a motorcyclist is trying to overtake you, you should
options: A) Drive faster to prevent the rider from overtaking you
B) Slow down and assist the rider to overtaking safely
C) Signal the driver to overtake on the left
questions.answer: B) Slow down and assist the rider to overtaking safely

questions.question: If the car you are overtaking is drifting in its lane, you should
options: A) Use your horn to warn him
B) Signal him with your hand
C) Overtake it quickly
questions.answer: A) Use your horn to warn him

questions.question: To drive in a way where other drivers will not find it necessary to overtake you, you should
options: A) Drive on the extreme right lane all the time
B) Always drive at a speed that match the traffic flow
C)Drive at the maximun speed limit of the road all the time
questions.answer: B) Always drive at a speed that match the traffic flow

questions.question: When a motorcyclist tries to overtake you on the left, you should
options: A) Increase your speed to race the rider.
B) Reduce your speed and assist the rider to overtake safely.
C) Ignore the rider and continue driving at your normal speed.
questions.answer: B) Reduce your speed and assist the rider to overtake safely.

questions.question: When another vehicle is overtaking you, you should
options: A) not speed up but assist him to overtake
B)change lane and keep to the right
C) increase your speed gradually
questions.answer: A) not speed up but assist him to overtake

questions.question: When being overtaken, you should
options: A) speed up
B) maintain your speed
C) slow down
questions.answer: C) slow down

questions.question: When the motorcycle you are overtaking suddenly increases speed, you should
options: A) accelerate more to overtake it quickly
B) slow down and abort overtaking it
C) sound your horn to warn the driver
questions.answer: B) slow down and abort overtaking it.

questions.question: When you have moved to the right hand side of the road to overtake another vehicle, you should
options: A) Maintain your normal speed and overtake as usual
B) Accelerate and overtake as quickly as possible
C) Decelerate and change to a higher gear
questions.answer: B) Accelerate and overtake as quickly as possible

questions.question: While overtaking another vehicle, the vehicle suddenly goes faster, you should
options: A) accelerate hard to overtake quickly
B) slow down and move safely back to your lane
C) sound the horn continuously to warn the other driver
questions.answer: B) slow down and move safely back to your lane

questions.question: Driving with a 'bald' tyre is dangerous because
options: A) it skids more easily.
B) there is greater probability of punctures.
C) both answers (A) and (B).
questions.answer: C) both answers (A) and (B).

questions.question: When you are driving along, you must check your rear view mirror once every
options: A) 1 to 2 seconds.
B) 5 to 10 seconds.
C) 20 to 30 seconds.
questions.answer: B) 5 to 10 seconds.

questions.question: Reversing from a side road into a main road is
options: A) Allowed if there is no vehicle around.
B) Not allowed for it is unsafe and could cause road accident.
C)Allowed during the daytime only.
questions.answer: B) Not allowed for it is unsafe and could cause road accident.

questions.question: You may overtake another vehicle on the left
options: A) If it is a heavy vehicle.
B) If the driver in front signals his intention to turn right.
C) If you are certain that the vehicle would not change direction.
questions.answer: B) If the driver in front signals his intention to turn right.

questions.question: Crossing the double continuous white lines along the centre of the road
options: A)Is an offence because it is unsafe to do so.
B) Is not an offence if you are overtaking another vehicle.
C) Is not an offence if you do not cause inconvenience to others.
questions.answer: A)Is an offence because it is unsafe to do so.

questions.question: No parking is allowed within ___ metres of a junction
options: A) 12 metres of a junction.
B) 6 metres of a junction.
C) 9 metres of a junction.
questions.answer: B) 6 metres of a junction.

questions.question: Parking of vehicle is prohibited within __ metres of a bus stop.
options: A) 15 metres of a bus stop.
B) 12 metres of a bus stop.
C) 9 metres of a bus stop.
questions.answer: C) 9 metres of a bus stop.

questions.question: When approaching a sharp bend or a steep hill, you
options: A) Should not overtake other vehicles.
B) May overtake other vehicles.
C) Should stay close behind the front vehicle.
questions.answer: A) Should not overtake other vehicles.

questions.question: When the vehicle you are overtaking suddenly increases its speed, you should
options: A) Increase your speed further.
B) Sound the horn and signal the driver to slow down.
C) Reduce your speed and return to your original lane.
questions.answer: C) Reduce your speed and return to your original lane.

questions.question: In traffic hold-ups, you should
options: A) try to get ahead of others by overtaking them on the right.
B) try to get ahead of others by overtaking them on the left.
C) stay in queue and follow the traffic flow.
questions.answer: C) stay in queue and follow the traffic flow.

questions.question: When you see a vehicle slowing down before a Zebra Crossing, you should
options: A) slow down and be prepared to stop.
B) sound the horn and signal the driver to slow down.
C) maintain your speed.
questions.answer: A) slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: Road hogging
options: A) allows others to overtake safely.
B) holds up the flow of traffic.
C) reduces road accident.
questions.answer: B) holds up the flow of traffic.

questions.question: You want to reverse into a side road.  You are not sure that the area behind your vehicle is clear.  What should you do?
options: A) carry on, assuming it is clear.
B) look through the rear window only.
C) get out and check.
questions.answer: C) get out and check.

questions.question: Before entering a round about, you should
options: A) Give way to traffic on your right.
B) Stop first before entering.
C) Accelerate to merge smoothly with traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.answer: A) Give way to traffic on your right.

questions.question: A tyre needs to be changed when
options: A) It is two years old.
B) The depth of its tread is less than 1.6 mm.
C) It is completely bald.
questions.answer: B) The depth of its tread is less than 1.6 mm.

questions.question: The minimum age requirement for applying for a Basic Theory Test is
options: A) 16 years.
B) 17 years.
C) 18 years.
questions.answer: C) 18 years.

questions.question: Unless otherwise stated, the maximum speed limit of all roads in Singapore is
options: A) 50km/h.
B) 60km/h.
C) 80km/h.
questions.answer: A) 50km/h.

questions.question: When driving in the rain, you should
options: A) Drive faster to get home.
B) Reduce your speed.
C) Drive at normal speed.
questions.answer: B) Reduce your speed.

questions.question: When driving pass pedestrians or cyclists, you should
options: A) Drive at normal speed, close to them.
B) Slow down and always give ample side clearance.
C) Drive quickly past them.
questions.answer: B) Slow down and always give ample side clearance.

questions.question: When following a bus that pulls up at a bus stop, you should
options: A) accelerate past the bus quickly.
B) slow down and watch carefully for pedestrians.
C) sound the horn and overtake the bus.
questions.answer: B) slow down and watch carefully for pedestrians.

questions.question: When the 'Red man' signal is on and pedestrians are crossing, you should
options: A) horn the pedestrians to demand the right of way.
B) stop and allow pedestrians to cross.
C) proceed behind the pedestrians.
questions.answer: B) stop and allow pedestrians to cross.

questions.question: When you see children standing by the side of the road, you should
options: A) maintain your normal speed.
B) slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.
C) speed pass them.
questions.answer: B) slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary

questions.question: You are driving pass a line of parked cars. You notice a ball bouncing out into the road ahead, you should
options: A) Continue driving at the same speed and sound your horn.
B) Slow down and be prepared to stop for children.
C) Continue driving at the same speed and try to avoid the ball.
questions.answer: B) slow down and be prepared to stop for children

questions.question: You are turning left into a side road.  Pedestrians are crossing the road near the junction.  You should
options: A) Wave them on.
B) Wait for them to cross.
C) Sound your horn.
questions.answer: B) Wait for them to cross.

questions.question: You need a longer distance to stop your vehicle when driving
options: A) On a dry road.
B) On a wet road.
C) On a hard and dry ground.
questions.answer: B) On a wet road.

questions.question: You see two elderly pedestrians about to cross the road ahead, you should
options: A) Expect them to wait for you to pass.
B) Speed up to pass them quickly.
C) Be careful, they may misjudge your speed.
questions.answer: C) Be careful, they may misjudge your speed.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect you?
options: A) It reduces your concentration.
B) It increases your awareness.
C) It improves your co-ordination.
questions.answer: A) It reduces your concentration.

questions.question: Drink driving
options: A) will not affect your reaction time.
B) may affect your reaction time.
C) may cause you to react faster.
questions.answer: B) may affect your reaction time.

questions.question: Which of the following statements on alcohol and driving is true?
options: A) It is safe to drive as long as you think you are not drunk.
B) It is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol.
C) It is safe to drive one hour after having the last drink.
questions.answer: B) It is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol.

questions.question: A person will be disqualified from driving if he is caught
options: A) Driving with a blood alcohol concentration over 80 mg of alcohol/100ml of  blood.
B) Failing to obey a 'Stop' traffic sign.
C) Failing to give way to an ambulance with its siren on.
questions.answer: A) Driving with a blood alcohol concentration over 80 mg of alcohol/100ml of  blood.

questions.question: A driver caught with a blood alcohol concentration over 80 mg of alcohol per 100 ml of blood will
options: A)have to pay a fine.
B) be charged in court.
C) be jailed.
questions.answer: B) be charged in court.

questions.question: After consuming alcohol, you should
options: A) not drive.
B) drive slowly.
C)drive at normal speed.
questions.answer: A) not drive.

questions.question: Any person caught driving with blood alcohol content which exceeds the prescribed  limit will
options: A) have to pay a fine.
B) be charged in court.
C) be given a warning.
questions.answer: B) be charged in court.

questions.question: Drink driving may cause
options: A) Reduce the co-ordination of the control of vehicle.
B) Faster reaction.
C) Increase alertness.
questions.answer: A) Reduce the co-ordination of the control of vehicle.

questions.question: Drinking and driving may cause
options: A) Increase confidence.
B) Loss of proper control of the vehicle.
C) Greater awareness of danger.
questions.answer: B) Loss of proper control of the vehicle.

questions.question: Generally, a small amount of alcohol can make you less safe on the road.
options: A) True.
B) False.
C) Not true, if you were an experience driver.
questions.answer: A) True

questions.question: How does the consumption of alcohol affect a person's driving?
options: A) It enables the driver to make better judgements.
B) It enables the driver to have better vision of the road.
C) It reduces the driver's reaction.
questions.answer: C) It reduces the driver's reaction.

questions.question: If you failed to have a proper control of your vehicle, you could be charged for _______________ even though your blood alcohol content is below the legal limit.
options: A) Careless driving.
B) Drink driving.
C) Reckless driving.
questions.answer: B) Drink driving.

questions.question: If you consume alcohol, you should
options: A) Have a coffee then drive home.
B) Go home by public transport.
C) Drive home carefully.
questions.answer: B) Go home by public transport.

questions.question: If you had too much alcohol,
options: A) your ability to drive is impaired.
B) Your reactions are better.
C) Your vision is improved.
questions.answer: A) your ability to drive is impaired.

questions.question: If you intend to drive after attending a function, you should
options: A) Avoid mixing your alcoholic drinks .
B) Avoid drinking alcohol.
C) Drink coffee before drinking alcohol.
questions.answer: B) Avoid drinking alcohol.

questions.question: The penalty for a repeat drink driving offender is
options: A) Fine, disqualification and a mandatory jail sentence.
B) Disqualification only.
C) Fine and disqualification only.
questions.answer: A) Fine, disqualification and a mandatory jail sentence.

questions.question: Drink driving can contribute to accidents because
options: A) Driver's judgement is impaired.
B) Drivers take shorter time to react.
C) Driver's vision is improved.
questions.answer: A) Driver's judgement is impaired.

questions.question: What advice should you give to a driver who has a few alcoholic drinks at a party?
options: A) Drive home carefully and slowly.
B) Go home by public transport.
C) Wait a short while and then drive home.
questions.answer: B) Go home by public transport.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences is TRUE?
options: A) Alcohol makes you a better driver.
B) Alcohol has no effect on the way you drive.
C) Alcohol slows down your reactions when driving.
questions.answer: C) Alcohol slows down your reactions when driving.

questions.question: Which of the following statement on alcohol is true?
options: A) You may decline a breath or blood test
B) Alcohol will not be detected by the breath test after peppermints have been eaten.
C) Even a small amount of alcohol tends to increase the chance of an accident.
questions.answer: C) Even a small amount of alcohol tends to increase the chance of an accident.

questions.question: Which of these can affect your reaction time?
options: A) Drugs
B) Contact lenses.
C) Tinted windows.
questions.answer: A) Drugs

questions.question: A passenger is exempted from wearing a seat belt if he is below
options: A) 1.7 metres in height.
B) 1.6 metres in height.
C) 1.5 metres in height.
questions.answer: C) 1.5 metres in height.

questions.question: Children passenger below _____ of age are required to use a child restraint.
options: A) 10 years.
B) 9 years.
C) 8 years.
questions.answer: C) 8 years.

questions.question: Fastening a seat belt can
options: A) Reduce the chances of a collision.
B) Reduce the chances of being seriously injured or killed.
C) Control your body movement when you negotiate a sharp bend.
questions.answer: B) Reduce the chances of being seriously injured or killed.

questions.question: Seat belt must be worn at all times by
options: A) the driver only.
B) the passengers only.
C) the driver as well as the passengers.
questions.answer: C) the driver as well as the passengers.

questions.question: A child is required to use a child restraint if the child is
options: A) 7 years old.
B) 9 years old.
C) 11 years old.
questions.answer: A) 7 years old.

questions.question: The 'Two-second Rule' is a sufficient distance between your vehicle and the car in front when road condition is
options: A) Wet.
B) Good.
C) Hazy.
questions.answer: B) Good.

questions.question: You are on a clear and open road in good weather condition, the distance between you and the vehicle in front should be
options: A) one car's length.
B) two car's length.
C) a two second time gap.
questions.answer: C) a two second time gap.

questions.question: The Two-second Rule is a simple check to ensure
options: A) A safe distance for you to move off from a junction.
B) A safe distance between your vehicle and the vehicle in front.
C) A safe length of time to signal before your manoeuvre.
questions.answer: B) A safe distance between your vehicle and the vehicle in front.

questions.question: When you are following another vehicle on a wet road, you should keep
options: A) 2 seconds behind.
B) More than 2 seconds behind.
C) Less than 2 seconds behind.
questions.answer: B) More than 2 seconds behind.

questions.question: The 'Two-Second Rule' of safe following distance applies to all vehicles travelling at
options: A) slow speed only.
B) fast speed  only.
C) any speed.
questions.answer: C) any speed.

questions.question: In order to avoid an accident with the vehicle in front while driving under normal conditions you should use the
options: A) Two-second rule
B) Four-second rule
C) Two metre rule
questions.answer: A) Two-second rule

questions.question: After driving through flood the brakes may malfunction. In order to correct this, you must
options: A) Stop the vehicle on a slope to allow water to flow out from the brakes.
B) Pump the brake pedal repeatedly to dry the brakes.
C) Drive at normal speed to spin-dry the brakes.
questions.answer: B) Pump the brake pedal repeatedly to dry the brakes.

questions.question: After your vehicle passed through a flood, you should
options: A) stop on a slope to drain water out of the brakes.
B) drive faster to allow the brakes to dry quickly.
C) apply intermittent braking to dry the brake drums at low speed.
questions.answer: C) apply intermittent braking to dry the brake drums at low speed.

questions.question: How should you deal with floods?
options: A) Drive through as fast as possible to avoid stopping.
B) Drive through slowly in 1st gear.
C) Drive through in the highest gear.
questions.answer: B) Drive through slowly in 1st gear.

questions.question: If you are in doubt of the depth of flood water (whether passable to vehicles), you should
options: A) Drive through slowly.
B) Drive through as quickly as possible.
C) Take an alternative route.
questions.answer: C) Take an alternative route.

questions.question: To drive through a flood, you should increase acceleration and
options: A) Change to a lower gear.
B) Change to a higher gear.
C) Apply half clutch.
questions.answer: A) Change to a lower gear.

questions.question: When approaching a road that is flooded but passable to vehicles, you should
options: A) Engage a higher gear to go through the flood.
B) Engage a lower gear to go through the flood.
C) Drive through as fast as possible.
questions.answer: B) Engage a lower gear to go through the flood.

questions.question: When driving in heavy rain and passing through water, you should gently test your
options: A) horn.
B) brakes from time to time.
C) signals.
questions.answer: B) brakes from time to time.

questions.question: All drivers are required by law to switch on the vehicle's headlights whilst driving between
options: A) 7.00 pm and 7.00 am.
B) 7.15 pm and 7.15 am.
C) 7.30 pm and 7.30 am.
questions.answer: A) 7.00 pm and 7.00 am.

questions.question: Switching on the headlights whilst driving in heavy rain during the daytime
options: A) Is advisable because you can be readily seen by others.
B) Is not advisable because it will shorten the battery life.
C) Is not advisable because the rain water will reflect the light.
questions.answer: A) Is advisable because you can be readily seen by others.

questions.question: At night, when approaching a sharp left bend you should
options: A) Flash your headlights to attract the attention of other road user.
B) Speed up so as to pass the danger as quickly as possible.
C) Keep more to the right to have a better view.
questions.answer: A) Flash your headlights to attract the attention of other road user.

questions.question: If the headlight of an oncoming vehicle is blinding you, you should
options: A) turn on the high beam.
B) look to the right kerb.
C) look to the left kerb.
questions.answer: C) look to the left kerb.

questions.question: At night you should switch on your headlights from
options: A) 6 pm to 7 am
B) 7 pm to 6 am
C) 7 pm to 7 am
questions.answer: C) 7 pm to 7 am

questions.question: In which situation should you switch on the high beam?
options: A) When driving on a bumpy road
B) When there are oncoming vehicles
C) When the road is poorly lighted and there is no traffic ahead
questions.answer: C) When the road is poorly lighted and there is no traffic ahead

questions.question: On a sharp bend at night, to avoid dazzling oncoming traffic, you should
options: A) Switch off your lights.
B) Dip your headlights.
C) Switch on high beam.
questions.answer: B) Dip your headlights.

questions.question: The purpose of using dipped headlights whilst driving is to
options: A) to save the battery's electrical energy.
B) to light up the road immediately in front of you.
C) to avoid dazzling drivers of oncoming vehicles.
questions.answer: C) to avoid dazzling drivers of oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: When blinded by the headlights of an oncoming vehicle at night, you should
options: A) Close your eyes.
B) Slow down or stop.
C) Pull down the sun visor.
questions.answer: B) Slow down or stop.

questions.question: When driving at night, dip your headlights-
options: A) To light up the road immediately in front you.
B) So as not to dazzle drivers of oncoming vehicles.
C) To prolong the life of the car battery.
questions.answer: B) So as not to dazzle drivers of oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should use
options: A) Dipped headlights.
B) High beam.
C) Side lights only.
questions.answer: A) Dipped headlights

questions.question: When facing oncoming traffic at night, which lights should you use?
options: A) Dipped headlights.
B) High beam headlights.
C) Spot lights.
questions.answer: A) Dipped headlights.

questions.question: When the oncoming car refuses to dim its headlights, you should
options: A) Slow down and look at the left side of the kerb
B) Retaliate by turning on your high beam.
C) Maintain your speed and the headlight status.
questions.answer: A) Slow down and look at the left side of the kerb

questions.question: You should dip your headlights when
options: A) Driving in a dark area.
B) Facing oncoming traffic.
C) Approaching a blind corner.
questions.answer: B) Facing oncoming traffic.
